_about: karma's reads on players that the numbers can't see. Kept by hand. 'motor': high-intensity player whose output rises with his minutes; never take an under on him when a starter at his position is out. 'small_ball_5': plays centre in small lineups, so there is rebound upside when the bigs sit. 'primary_guard_defender': guards the opponent's main ball-handler, so his minutes hold up whatever happens to his shooting. 'rebounds_suppressed_with_giannis': fade this player's rebound overs when Giannis plays. 'low_mistake_trusted': the coach trusts him and his minutes are steady, but his output moves between stats, so prefer combo props. 'big_game_closer': plays more and is on the floor at the end of close or big games. Team tag 'trapping_defense' (karma, 8 Nov): good defences come in two styles. TRAPPING (DET, TOR, CLE lately, OKC historically) forces turnovers by pressuring the playmaker; CONTAINING (SAS, current OKC) contests and stays home and forces few. Only trapping moves playmakers' TOV/AST props.

OKC.note: karma, 7 Nov: with SGA and whoever else, OKC know how to win; they have won through constant lineup changes for two seasons. Measured (SGA's game logs): with SGA playing and one of Holmgren / J. Williams missing, 38-7 in 2024-25 and 40-5 in 2025-26; with both missing 5-0 and 5-1 (3-2 so far in 2026-27). So do not let our absence penalty sink OKC's team total/margin the way it would for a normal team; their system holds. Example (karma, verified in game logs): 9 Mar 2026 v DEN, OKC beat Jokic's Nuggets without J. Williams, Holmgren, Caruso AND Hartenstein; SGA 35/9/15 with 0 TO, tying Wilt's 126 straight 20-point games. Thunder Collective (6 Nov): Caruso back; new pieces Micah Peavy (POA defender) and Dalen Terry; Jaylin Williams out (back spasms). OKC lack wing size, so Cam Boozer could give them problems; Mara likely draws Edey/Boozer. Reporters expect a close OKC win at MEM with SGA closing (MEM's only closer is Jerome). Next: WAS on the 2nd night of a back-to-back (Caruso may rest), then POR twice in Portland. Hoop Collective (7 Nov): OKC lost three all-defensive players (Holmgren 8-10 weeks, Wallace, J. Williams); their defence was their offence (1st in points off turnovers each of the last 3 seasons) but they are about 22nd in the 6 games since. So SGA now works against set half-court defences loaded up on him; teams make Ajay Mitchell beat them. Discount OKC's season turnover/fast-break numbers in game_lens. karma, 7 Nov: the short-handed group is LEARNING to play together, so season-to-date stats since the injuries understate them. Example: ranked ~22nd in forcing turnovers since the injuries, then 17 pts off turnovers by halftime at MEM (7 Nov). Weight their most recent games over the post-injury average. karma, 8 Nov: OKC started Hartenstein + Aday Mara together (McCain to bench) vs WAS without AD: 'for a good start and collecting data points with the double-big lineup'. Treat early double-big games as experiments: track minutes together, rebound margin and +/- before it changes Hartenstein REB / Mara / McCain props. 8 Nov vs WAS: 3rd straight opponent held to a season-low FG% (WAS 30%, OKC by 39). Double big result: Hartenstein 14 reb in 18 min, Mara 18p 8r in 27 min. karma: when Chet returns, Hartenstein's role holds (9.2 reb with Chet in 2025-26 vs 10.1 without), Mara keeps developmental minutes, and Hartenstein/Chet foul trouble gives Mara a significant role (a live-bet spot vs foul-drawing bigs). karma, 8 Nov: be careful picking props in OKC games. Overs on OKC's OPPONENTS only when that team has what beats them (shot creators who score without turnovers, a middle game, size that rebounds). Held 3 straight opponents to season-low FG%. karma, 8 Nov: OKC's passing-lane scheme (Wallace, J-Dub, Caruso) led the league in forced TOV in 2024-25 and 2025-26 (15.7/g both). 2026-27 fell to 21st (14.0): 26 Oct-4 Nov only 7-12 forced, 3-8 steals; last two (MEM 18 forced/10 stl, WAS 11/9 stl) show it returning. Check whether the dip lines up with Caruso's absence. karma, 8 Nov: that turnover edge is why OKC blow teams out: they force turnovers on opposing guards while SGA is one of the least turnover-prone high-usage guards (measured: 3rd-lowest TOV rate of the top-20 usage players in 2026-27, 2.2/g; 2nd in 2025-26). OKC TOV margin +3.8/g in 2025-26 (1st), +2.0 in 2026-27 (7th) so far.

So fade Bam's rebound overs when Giannis plays; Giannis's rebound overs look better. karma: he is still scoring (7 pts in Q1). The role moves his output from rebounds to points, so his points overs are fine and rebounds are the stat to fade. karma's rule: if we bet Bam, it has to be points + rebounds (PR), and only if the line is decent. No pure rebound props while he plays the 4 beside Giannis. karma (Q4, 5 Nov US): twice he was under the basket and made no effort for the rebound. He looks to be boxing out and leaving the board to Giannis, or is tired on the second night of a back-to-back after OT. Either way the rebound fade is real. Result 5 Nov: 18 pts, 10 reb in 33 min, so the rebound over still landed despite the low-effort stretches. MIA staggered him with Giannis (Giannis back in for Bam late Q1 and late Q2), so Bam gets solo-big minutes each half. Treat one game's effort read as a reason to prefer PR, not as a reason to bet the rebound under.

Points overs ride volume; efficiency-dependent props (FG made, 3PM) less so. karma, 7 Nov: never bet Shai unders (any stat, incl. quarter props like 1Q points). MEASURED 7 Nov (ESPN PBP): 2026-27 by quarter avg 5.8 / 6.5 / 11.1 / 6.8 (1Q 9,0,5,2,4,8,9,9; Q3 is his biggest quarter, 37% of his points); first shot usually 1.5-4 min in. Last 12 games of 2025-26: 1Q 8.0 (28%), 10+ in 3 of 12. Read CONFIRMED: slow starter, third-quarter scorer. karma, 8 Nov: uses aggressive defence against you by drawing fouls. Measured vs the 8 most turnover-forcing teams: 2025-26 10.6 FTA/32.5 pts/2.2 TOV (n=21) vs 8.7/29.8/2.4 otherwise; 2024-25 9.7 FTA vs 8.7. vs DET: 48 (15 Mar 2025; Bickerstaff 'disgusted' by officiating, 5 of SGA's 10 FTA from DET technicals), 47 with 21/25 FT and Ausar fouled out (30 Mar 2026). CORRECTION karma, 8 Nov: the complaints have worked: 2026-27 FTA 6.8/g, FTr 0.29 (n=10) vs 9.2/0.47 in 2025-26 and 8.9/0.41 in 2024-25. OKC team FTA 27th this season (15th, 17th before). The real foul story was OKC's opponents: 4th-most opp FTA in 2024-25 (Finch: 'they foul a ton').
